title: Atheism, Orthodoxy or Catholicism: which premises and which numbers does each conclusion actually depend on, once the arguments are machine-checked and the evidence is a likelihood-ratio ledger?
lede: research programme: 11 arguments for and against God and between Rome and Orthodoxy machine-checked with their cruxes computed (the modal ontological argument needs system B, its atheist mirror only T); in a sourced Bayes-factor ledger the resurrection testimony carries 98.5% of the variance on Christianity and needs a Bayes factor of only about 7 under even priors, while the prior outweighs every theism-vs-naturalism evidence item
summary: An open programme that puts the case between naturalism, Eastern Orthodox Christianity and Catholicism into two checkable forms. Logic: a stdlib decision procedure (S5 exact by Ladner’s bound; monadic first-order exact by a small-model argument) decides 11 arguments and computes their minimal inconsistent premise sets, with Lean 4 versions of each proof. All are valid as stated, so validity never settles anything. The Hartshorne–Plantinga modal ontological argument needs a symmetric accessibility relation (valid in B and S5, two-world countermodels in T and S4), while its reverse (“possibly no maximally great being exists”) is valid already in T. The Honorius and Florence disputes have exactly two minimal inconsistent sets and 16 coherent positions; Catholicism and Orthodoxy each drop two claims. Evidence: a 13-item likelihood-ratio ledger, each entry labelled published, argued or swept, reproduces Unwin’s 67% exactly. The resurrection testimony carries 98.5% of the variance of Christianity-vs-rest log odds; the Bayes factor it needs for P(Christian) > 0.5 is 7.3 under even priors (0.5 to 294 across a 3×3 prior grid), between a sceptic’s 1 and the ~1044 reported for the McGrews. For theism vs naturalism the prior carries 54% of the variance and swept fine-tuning 31%. Milestone 2: a leave-one-out shows the midpoint P(naturalism) of 0.76 rests on three items (dropping natural evil, moral evil or hiddenness each takes it to 0.5 or below), which the variance shares alone hide; and an exhaustive S5 model search finds Scott’s version of Gödel’s argument satisfiable only in one-world models (modal collapse). A proof (E10) then characterises every finite model of Anderson’s repair: a model exists exactly when the property algebra has a block made of whole individuals, so the God-like individual has no contingent property and no contingent proposition is expressible as a property; exhaustive search agrees on all 563 algebras checked. Limits: most ranges are swept, not sourced; the church-level ratios are symmetric placeholders until elicited; the Lean files were not compiled in this session; the McGrews’ figure is a secondary report. These are model outputs given stated inputs, not findings about whether God exists.
